artifacts.summary: Full implementation summary covering all 8 phases, decisions, deviations, and the honest complete-gate-set verification account.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented verify-touched.sh (the single touched-path narrowing entry point), its declarable resolver interface, the classified NO-SUITE-BY-CLASS/OWED-NOT-PAID fallback, the coverage convergence report, owed-sweep discharge at the batch gate, and the authoring/dispatch surface rewrite naming verify-touched.sh as the one narrowing command -- all 8 plan phases complete, redeployed clean (41/41 fast checks); the complete gate set surfaced 2 confirmed pre-existing, task-unrelated failures and 1 load-induced flake, logged via issue-record.sh and left unfixed as out of scope.

memory_candidates.content: lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh's MISSING-DECLARATION check counts `grep -c common_test_resolve_subject` vs `grep -c common_test_declare_subject` ACROSS THE WHOLE FILE, including comments. A header comment that spells out 'common_test_resolve_subject' by name (common when documenting the technique) inflates the resolve-count past the declare-count and trips a false VIOLATION even when every real call is correctly paired. Fix: describe the mechanism in prose without repeating the literal function identifier, or add a throwaway extra common_test_declare_subject call.

A checked-in glob-matched data file keying on a touched-path string (e.g. suite-selection-map.data, suite-selection-noclass.data) must use REPO-ROOT-RELATIVE path globs, never a sub-tree-relative shorthand -- `git diff --name-only` (and any git-ls-files-based enumeration) always returns repo-root-relative paths regardless of invocation cwd, and a bash glob match (`[[ path == glob ]]`) requires the exact base to line up. Authoring rows while manually testing from within a subdirectory can silently bake in the wrong base; verify against the real derivation path (git diff from the repo root), not a convenient manual-test shorthand.

For a fast, deterministic test of a script that wraps run-all.sh (or any other heavyweight battery runner), stub the wrapped script entirely: have the stub record every argument it received to a marker file beside itself and return a controllable pass/fail via a toggle file, rather than copying the real ~200-suite corpus into a fixture. This lets the test assert on the WRAPPER's own constructed invocation (presence/absence of --only, --cost-class, etc.) directly, in milliseconds, without paying the real battery's cost -- precedent: test-gate8-suite-selection.sh's stubbed run-all.sh.

sapience_notes.subject: suite-resolver-lib.sh's union-escalation avoidance
sapience_notes.value: suite_resolver_resolve calls suite_selection_select/suite_selection_unmapped ONE PATH AT A TIME rather than multi-path, specifically to avoid suite-selection-lib.sh's own union-escalation rule (one unmappable path among several escalates the WHOLE call to __FULL_SWEEP__). No edit to suite-selection-lib.sh was needed; this is purely a different call pattern over its existing, unchanged public functions.

sapience_notes.subject: lint-subject-resolution-declaration.sh detection method
sapience_notes.value: The MISSING-DECLARATION check is a naive grep -c count of the literal strings common_test_resolve_subject and common_test_declare_subject across a whole test-suite file, including comments -- a comment that names the resolve function for documentation purposes can falsely trip the lint even when every real call is correctly paired with a declaration.

sapience_notes.subject: touched-path glob data files (suite-selection-map.data, suite-selection-noclass.data)
sapience_notes.value: Their path_glob column must be REPO-ROOT-RELATIVE, matching git diff --name-only's own always-repo-root-relative output, never a sub-tree-relative shorthand convenient for manual testing from within a subdirectory. A mismatch silently makes every row fail to match in real use while still appearing to work under a manual test run from the wrong cwd.

sapience_notes.subject: lint-agent-contracts.sh's scan scope for NO-SUITE-BY-CLASS classification
sapience_notes.value: An existing agent-definition markdown file (e.g. agents/general-implementation-agent.md) is NOT a reliable NO-SUITE-BY-CLASS probe, because suite-selection-lib.sh's grep-based reference stratum already resolves it via existing fixtures that mention its filename -- it never reaches the classified fallback at all. Only a genuinely new, unreferenced agent-file path exercises that classification branch.

sapience_notes.subject: report-suite-coverage.sh's read-only design
sapience_notes.value: report-suite-coverage.sh deliberately re-implements the NO-SUITE-BY-CLASS glob lookup locally rather than calling unmapped-fallback-lib.sh's public unmapped_fallback_classify, because that function also WRITES a durable owed record for every OWED path -- calling it from a whole-tree advisory scan would spuriously populate records/full-sweep-owed.jsonl for the entire unconverged backlog on every run.

sapience_notes.subject: owed-sweep discharge gating in orchestrate-batch-gate.sh
sapience_notes.value: Owed-record discharge is gated on the WHOLE batch-gate run's gate_exit_code, never per-task: an owed path is owed against 'the complete gate set passing', so a failure anywhere in that run -- even one attributed to a different task -- means the obligation is not yet met for any task, not only the one that caused the failure.

sapience_notes.subject: pre-existing, task-650-unrelated gate-8 failures as of this task's completion
sapience_notes.value: test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh (validate-artifact.sh's SKILL_VALIDATE_FIXES/SKILL_VALIDATE_FIXED_FILES globals reporting 0 fixes where cases 3/4/6/6b expect nonzero) and test-mcp-merge-target.sh (a hand-written .mcp.json entry not surviving a force-reload/regenerate cycle, assertions C and E) both fail reproducibly in isolation on this repository as of 2026-11-19, confirmed via git log to be unrelated to task 650 (neither suite nor its subjects were ever touched by that task's commits). Logged via issue-record.sh; not fixed.
